Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second innings! Now, as Zimbabwe prepare to bat in their first innings, they find themselves under a mountain of pressure. The pitch is still decent for batting, but the scoreboard pressure is enormous. South Africa will look to attack early with their pace battery and spin options, hoping to snatch a couple of wickets before tea. The two openers of Zimbabwe have come out, where Takudzwanashe Kaitano will open the inning alongside Dion Myers. Codi Yusuf has the new ball in his hands and he will start the proceedings. Here we go...
... Second Innings ...

Mulder’s innings will go down as one of the great Test knocks in recent memory. He resumed Day 2 on 264 unbeaten and never looked in trouble. Calm, commanding, and classy, as he became only the second South African after Hashim Amla to score a triple century in Test cricket. He hit 49 fours and 4 sixes in his monumental 367 off 334 deliveries, striking at over 100 for the bulk of his innings. His ability to maintain high intensity over such a long knock speaks volumes about his fitness and mindset. From Zimbabwe’s point of view, it was a painful two days in the field. They started promisingly with early wickets, and Tanaka Chivanga was their pick of the bowlers, getting two crucial scalps and maintaining decent control. Kundai Matigimu also picked up two but went for runs. Wellington Masakadza, after his early wicket, lacked consistency and went for 184 runs in his 33 overs. The likes of Muzarabani and Madhevere were rendered ineffective as the South African batters dismantled every bowling plan with ruthless efficiency. Zimbabwe’s fielding was also sloppy at times, which only made things worse.

The innings began shakily for the Proteas. Tony de Zorzi was dismissed early after edging to slip, and debutant Lesego Senokwane couldn’t hold on for long either, trapped LBW by Wellington Masakadza for just 3 runs. At 24/2, Zimbabwe had their tails up and looked poised to make early inroads. But the early optimism quickly faded as Wiaan Mulder and David Bedingham came together and started to shift gears. Their counterattack began subtly but grew in confidence, with both batters picking boundaries at will and rotating strike effortlessly. By the time Bedingham fell LBW for a well-made 82, they had stitched an 184-run partnership, flipping the pressure entirely back onto the Zimbabweans. The baton was then passed to young Lhuan-dre Pretorius, who played with maturity beyond his age. Partnering with a rock-solid Mulder, they built another massive stand of 217 runs. Lhuan looked fluent and fearless, playing attractive shots, including three sixes in his knock of 78. His innings gave South Africa the luxury of controlling the pace of the game while Mulder continued to bat like a man possessed. Though Lhuan missed out on his century, the damage was already done by the time he fell to Matigimu. The Zimbabwean bowlers looked deflated and out of plan.

The news has come in just that, South Africa have declared after a dominating first innings performance, amassing a massive total of 626/5 in just 114 overs, a statement of intent if ever there was one. Put in to bat on Day 1 by Zimbabwe, the visitors didn’t start well and found themselves at 24/2 in the morning session. But what followed was an absolute carnage with the bat. Wiaan Mulder led from the front with an extraordinary triple century, supported brilliantly by Bedingham, Lhuan-dre, and Verreynne. Zimbabwe started well but faded rapidly as South Africa turned the game into a run-fest. With this declaration, they’ve not only drained the energy out of the Zimbabwean attack but also put themselves in complete control of the match.
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

The stage is set for an intriguing post-lunch session. Will Mulder reach the milestone, or will Zimbabwe's bowlers find a way to break through? The Proteas' batting dominance has been impressive, but Zimbabwe will be eager to stop Wiaan Mulder from creating another bit of history. We'll be back with ball-to-ball coverage at 10.40 am GMT to see how the action unfolds!

Zimbabwe did manage to break the partnership, with Kundai Matigimu removing Brevis for 30. Kyle Verreynne joined Mulder and has played solidly, scoring 42. Despite this small success for Zimbabwe, the Proteas continued to dominate, and it's clear that Mulder's pursuit of Brian Lara's record of an unbeaten 400 is the only thing standing in the way of a declaration.

Sheer dominance from South Africa as they own the first session on Day 2 as well. The Proteas picked up where they left off on Day 1, with Dewald Brevis smashing the first ball of Day 2 for a boundary. The visitors dominated the morning session, adding 161 runs in 26 overs. Wiaan Mulder continued his incredible form, stretching his overnight score of 264 to become South Africa's top scorer in Test cricket, now unbeaten on 367.

Commentary.Commentary: The stage is set for Day 2! Dewald Brevis will face the first ball, with Wiaan Mulder at the other end. Blessing Muzarabani will start proceedings for Zimbabwe. Can the Zimbabwean bowlers finally break through and give their team a good start on Day 2? The Proteas, meanwhile, will be looking to build on their impressive Day 1 total. Let's see how things unfold!

David Bedingham is up for a quick chat before the match. He says that the pitch in this Test felt much easier compared to the first one, and his approach was simply to bat with confidence. He’s pleased to have built a solid partnership and helped set the tone. Adds that playing off the back foot was more comfortable, though Blessing Muzarabani, with his height, was getting some extra bounce, which made things tricky at times. He mentions that he looked to be more aggressive and is thankful it paid off. Praises the captain’s knock, saying it was on another level and made the ball look like a football with the way he timed it. Talks about a discussion they had in the dressing room, how to go after the good-length deliveries and not let the bowlers settle. Ends by saying that the plan is to bat long, which should rough up the surface and hopefully bring the spinners into play from day three.

Blessing Muzarabani of Zimbabwe is up for a chat. He reflects on his performance, starting by saying that the wicket behaved slightly differently compared to the last Test, with the ball doing just a little bit more off the surface. He adds that using the short ball is one of his strengths, but he made a few adjustments to his approach this time to make it more effective. Mentions that playing so much cricket can be physically demanding, and finding ways to take wickets on such surfaces is always a challenge. Emphasises the importance of knowing your strengths, focusing more on the off-stump line, pitching it full but avoiding half-volleys. He admits yesterday was tough, but remains hopeful that they’ll put on a better show today.

Day 2 promises to be a fascinating contest, with Mulder chasing history and Zimbabwe determined to stop him. Can the Proteas continue their dominance, or will Zimbabwe find a way to turn the tide? Let's see how the day unfolds!

The task for Zimbabwe is to take wickets or restrict the flow of runs to create opportunities. The Zimbabwean bowlers had a tough day on Day 1, but they'll be well-rested and eager to bounce back. Tanaka Chivanga was the pick of the bowlers on Day 1, and they'll be looking to make early inroads today.

Mulder had able support from his teammates, with David Bedingham scoring 82 and Lhuan-dre Pretorius chipping in with 78. Now, he's partnered with Dewald Brevis, who plays aggressively. South Africa seems to be aiming to bat Zimbabwe out of the contest, and with their firepower, they're likely targeting a massive total of at least 650.

Welcome to Day 2 of the 2nd Test between Zimbabwe and South Africa! The stage is set for another thrilling day of cricket, with South Africa dominating the proceedings on Day 1. They finished the day at 465/4, with Wiaan Mulder leading the charge with an unbeaten 264. The big question on everyone's mind is, can he break Brian Lara's record of 400? If he stays out for more than one session, he'll be in with a strong chance.

The Zimbabwean bowlers will need to regroup and come out firing on Day 2 if they want even a glimmer of hope to stay in the game. They gave away too many boundary-hitting deliveries, which proved costly. Tanaka Chivanga was the pick of the bowlers, claiming two wickets, while Kundai Matigimu and Wellington Masakadza got one each. Day 2 promises to be crucial, and Zimbabwe will need to make early inroads to stay in contention. The action for Day 2 will begin at 8 am GMT tomorrow, Monday, 7th July, but you can join us an hour earlier for all the buildup. Cheers for now!

The partnership of 184 runs between Mulder and David Bedingham (82) laid the foundation, and later Mulder and Lhuan-dre Pretorius (78) took the score to new heights with a 217-run stand for the fourth wicket. These back-to-back marathon partnerships tore apart Zimbabwe's bowling attack. Mulder's maiden double ton was the highlight, and he got a lucky escape later in the day when he was bowled off a no-ball on 247, which will surely rankle Zimbabwe.

BAD LIGHT STOPS PLAY AND IT IS STUMPS ON DAY 1. What a day it has been in Bulawayo! Wiaan Mulder will surely remember this day for a long time, scoring an unbeaten 264. Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! South Africa have gone past the 300-run mark and are now pushing towards a potential 400-plus total by stumps on Day 1. With just the final hour remaining, skipper Wiaan Mulder is charging towards what could be his second century of the series, showcasing both class and composure. Lhuan-dre Pretorius has played the perfect supporting role, as he is just 2 runs away from his half-century, and together, the duo has already stitched a partnership of 131 runs. On the other side, Zimbabwe’s bowling attack has lacked bite, failing to build pressure or create consistent chances, even letting a key opportunity slip away. All eyes are now on this closing phase of the day, which could set the tone for the remainder of the match.

Commentary.Commentary: Back for the third and final session of the day! The crowd has gathered in good numbers and there out walk the unbeaten batters of South Africa, where the centurion skipper Wiaan Mulder will resume the inning alongside young Lhuan-dre Pretorius. Tanaka Chivanga will start the proceedings. Here we go...
... Day 1, Session 3 ...

With Lhuan-dre Pretorius joining Wiaan Mulder and Dewald Brevis waiting in the wings, Zimbabwe need to be on high alert to prevent a batting explosion. Will the Proteas unleash a flurry of runs, putting Zimbabwe on the back foot, or will the Zimbabwean bowlers tighten up and claim crucial wickets? The answer hangs in the balance, making for an intriguing third session on Day 1. Join us at 1.01 pm GMT for the final session.

Zimbabwe's chances are slipping away due to crucial errors, like giving away easy singles to David Bedingham and Wiaan Mulder. To turn things around, they need to learn from these mistakes and apply pressure on the Proteas' batting unit going forward. Failure to do so might make it extremely difficult for them to get back into the game, even though it's still early on Day 1 of the 2nd Test. Tanaka Chivanga has looked the best by some margin and others like Blessing Muzarabani and Wellington Masakadza need to step up and support the pacer.

The Proteas dominated the second session, adding 130 runs in 28 overs at a scoring rate of 4.64. Wiaan Mulder and David Bedingham continued where they left off, stretching their partnership to 184 before Bedingham fell 18 runs short of his century. Mulder remained unstoppable, reaching 133 unbeaten at the break. New batter in line, Lhuan-dre Pretorius quickly made his mark, scoring a run a ball 13, with the Proteas looking set to pile up a massive total.

Commentary.Commentary: Back for the second session! The umpires are back in the middle, and so are the players of Zimbabwe, who get in a huddle, where the skipper Craig Ervine gives a pep talk, and now they are spreading out to take their respective positions. Two unbeaten players of South Africa, the skipper Wiaan Mulder and David Bedingham, are also out and would want to get going. Tanaka Chivanga will start the proceedings. Here we go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

Heading into the second session, South Africa will look to build on this strong foundation. With two set batters at the crease and plenty of stroke-makers still to come, they’ll eye a big total. Zimbabwe, meanwhile, need quick wickets after lunch to bring themselves back into the game. The pitch looks decent for batting, but the odd ball is doing just enough to keep the bowlers interested. Join us at 10.40 am GMT for the next post-lunch session.

From Zimbabwe’s point of view, the session started promisingly, but they let it slip away in the second half. Tanaka Chivanga was the standout bowler, picking up the wicket of de Zorzi and keeping the batters honest with a probing line. Blessing Muzarabani, despite not getting a wicket, bowled four maiden overs on the trot, and created chances, including the dropped catch. Zimbabwe even tried a short-ball strategy to rattle both these batters, but Mulder and Bedingham were up for the challenge.

Wiaan Mulder batted like a man on a mission in his first outing as a Test skipper. He reached his half-century in just 53 balls, peppering the boundary regularly with crisp drives, confident pulls, and one authoritative six. David Bedingham supported him brilliantly from the other end. His approach was fearless and fluent, hitting boundaries at will and quickly getting into rhythm. Bedingham raced to 40 off just 34 balls, and his strike rate tells the story of how South Africa turned a cautious start into a dominating end to the session.

Tony de Zorzi and Lesego Senokwane, the debutant, struggled early on as Zimbabwe’s bowlers made good use of the helpful conditions. De Zorzi, in particular, had a nervy start and was dropped at second Sean Williams when he was on just 4. But he couldn't capitalise on the reprieve and eventually got out for just 10. Senokwane, on the other end, barely got going and looked tentative in his first outing. He was pinned LBW by Wellington Masakadza for just 3. With both openers back in the hut for just 24 runs on the board, it felt like South Africa could tumble early. However, the arrival of Bedingham at the crease changed the tempo completely.

It was a session that swung like a pendulum, starting in Zimbabwe’s favour before South Africa clawed their way back with authority. Zimbabwe won the toss and chose to field, and for the first hour, they held all the aces. Their bowlers stuck to a nagging line and length, keeping things tight and challenging the batters with movement and discipline. South Africa were reeling at 24 for 2, and it looked like they were in for a long grind. But the tide turned sharply when Wiaan Mulder and David Bedingham came together and stitched an unbeaten partnership of 89 runs in just 85 balls, shifting momentum back to the Proteas. The last 10 overs alone fetched 52 runs without loss, highlighting the shift in control. South Africa go into lunch at 113 for 2 in 28 overs, ending the session firmly in the driver’s seat.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! Zimbabwe have been spot on with their line and length from the very first over, and their disciplined bowling has earned them two big wickets early on, removing both South African openers within the opening hour. With the momentum on their side, they'll be eager to strike again before lunch and firmly stamp their authority on this opening session of the second Test. On the other hand, South Africa found themselves under pressure despite a cautious approach at the top. Their openers looked to weather the new ball but eventually fell in the process. Now, with early breakthroughs setting the tone, the next phase promises to be a gripping battle. With that, David Bedingham walks out to bat next.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the action to kick off. The players of Zimbabwe get in a huddle, led by their skipper, Craig Ervine before they spread out to take their respective positions. Also, the umpires come out and so are the openers of South Africa, where Tony de Zorzi will open the innings alongside debutant Lesego Senokwane. Blessing Muzarabani has the new ball in his hands and he will start the proceedings with three slips and a gully. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Shaun Pollock is pitchside alongside Ed Rainsford. According to Ed Rainsford and Shaun Pollock, the pitch is batting-friendly with minimal grass in the middle. They expect little movement for seamers but possible spin later on. The first hour will be crucial, and overall, the conditions favour the batters.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Tony de Zorzi, Lesego Senokwane (On Debut) (In for Matthew Breetzke), Wiaan Mulder (C), David Bedingham, Lhuan-dre Pretorius, Dewald Brevis, Kyle Verreynne (WK), Senuran Muthusamy (In for Keshav Maharaj), Corbin Bosch, Prenelan Subrayen (On Debut) (In for Kwena Maphaka), Codi Yusuf.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Dion Myers (In for Prince Masvaure), Takudzwanashe Kaitano, Nick Welch, Sean Williams, Craig Ervine (C), Wessly Madhevere, Tafadzwa Tsiga (WK), Wellington Masakadza, Kundai Matigimu (On Debut) (In for Vincent Masekesa), Blessing Muzarabani, Tanaka Chivanga.

The skipper of South Africa, Wiaan Mulder, calls it an extremely proud moment for him and his family to lead South Africa in Test cricket. He says he feels fortunate to have a few players in the squad who’ve been alongside him since their U19 days, making it extra special. Mentions that after a few days off, the team has regrouped well and bonded off the field. He confirms a few changes in the playing XI, with some new faces coming in, where Lesego Senokwane and Prenelan Subrayen are making their debuts, and says it’s part of the plan as they prepare for the sub-continent, aiming to give the spinners more game time. The pitch, he adds, tends to flatten out and should assist the spinners as the match progresses. He praises the pace unit for their ability to bowl long spells regardless of the surface and says they were looking to bat first anyway, so losing the toss works perfectly.

The skipper of Zimbabwe, Craig Ervine, says that they have opted to bowl first to capitalise on the morning conditions with an extra seamer in the lineup. He acknowledges the absence of an additional seamer in the first Test, which might have made a difference after a promising start with the new ball. Ervine emphasises the importance of basics and execution, highlighting a positive team mood with focused training sessions. The team aims to improve on their plans and performance in the first Test. Informs that Kundai Matigimu replaces Vincent Masekesa, making his debut, while Dion Myers takes Prince Masvaure's place, who is out due to illness.
TOSS - Zimbabwe have won the toss and they have opted to BOWL first.
